title: Consolidated App-Level Docs Import Delivery
summary: replace context-filtered Import and separate Review package entrypoints with one app-level staged-source chooser
content_html:
Consolidated App-Level Docs Import Delivery

Status And Purpose

Started as CAI-1 under Roadmap. CAI-1.0 is complete and at its review gate. CAI-1.1 remains unstarted.

CAI-1 replaces separate parent-scope Import, sub-scope report Import, and Review package entrypoints with one manage-only app-level Import action. The chooser lists every recognized staged document candidate without filtering the list by the currently displayed scope or sub-scope.

The selected source kind decides how its destination is resolved:

  • an ordinary standalone document imports into the frozen current display context; and
  • a trusted package or edited review-source folder imports into the exact collection declared by its associated trusted manifest and metadata.

Prepare Package remains a separate checked-document action. Docs Review remains optional.

Complete Outcome

One app-level Import action opens a shared staged-source modal from any local Manage Docs Viewer state.

The modal:

  1. lists every recognized ordinary document, returned package, and edited review-source folder in Import staging;
  2. does not filter that inventory by the displayed context;
  3. has no Import type or Publish into dropdown;
  4. shows each source kind and its read-only effective destination;
  5. offers Open in Docs Review only for a server-declared reviewable returned package;
  6. previews and confirms Import through the existing ordinary or collection workflow; and
  7. ends with an explicit link to the exact destination affected by the result.

The selected candidate already determines the Import workflow. Its destination is either the frozen display context for an ordinary document or the trusted manifest target for a package, so neither value is user-selectable.

Standalone image, SVG, Mermaid, downloadable, and other media files are ignored by Import. They remain owned by the Source editor's Add image… and Add file… workflows.

Candidate Model

“Package” means a staged source with an associated trusted manifest or metadata record linked through export_id and the existing package provenance contract. Filename shape, extension, directory shape, or the mere presence of an unvalidated manifest.json does not grant package behavior.

candidate kind destination authority Import Open in Docs Review
ordinary DOCX, HTML, Markdown, text, or one-document Markdown folder frozen current display context create-only disabled
trusted returned JSON/JSONL package associated trusted manifest and metadata according to supports_return_import according to supports_docs_review
complete edited review-source folder retained review manifest and trusted export metadata overwrite-only disabled
invalid, incomplete, unsupported, or capability-blocked candidate none disabled with reason disabled

The server projects candidate kind, validation state, capabilities, target mode, exact target, display label, and disabled reason. The browser does not infer them from filenames or reconstruct manifest associations.

The capability rule remains fail closed:

  • supports_docs_review: true enables Open in Docs Review for a valid returned package;
  • supports_return_import: true enables Import for a valid package and exact eligible collection;
  • false / true remains invalid; and
  • a complete edited review-source folder is already the output of the review workflow, so it never receives another Review action.

An ordinary one-document Markdown folder remains an ordinary create-only source. Being folder-shaped does not make it a trusted package.

Package Naming

Newly prepared document package names do not repeat the document domain:

  • a package file uses {timestamp}-{profile_id}.{format}, for example 20260730-095512-document-content.jsonl; and
  • its retained review package id and folder use {timestamp}-{profile_id}, for example 20260730-095512-document-content.

The profile ids remain document-content and document-tree. Trusted metadata still carries adapter_id: documents, data_domain: documents, profile_id, and export_id; removing the redundant physical-name segment does not change trusted export identity, validation, capability, or routing authority.

This is a forward-only naming change. CAI-1 does not migrate, alias, or preserve compatibility for files or review folders already staged under {timestamp}-documents-{profile_id}; they may be cleared and regenerated.

Listing Contract

The app-level listing is context-independent:

  • every recognized document candidate appears from parent-scope, sub-scope report, and sub-scope detail states;
  • package rows retain their manifest-owned destination even when another collection is displayed;
  • ordinary rows show the frozen current-context destination supplied for this modal session;
  • invalid claimed packages remain visible but disabled when the service can provide a safe diagnostic;
  • standalone media and unrelated drop-zone files are omitted; and
  • recognition still runs before generic Markdown normalization so review_* and package provenance cannot be stripped before classification.

Removing list filtering does not weaken source validation or expose arbitrary filesystem paths. Candidates remain confined to the configured shared staging root and retain their exact staged request identities.

Ordinary Document Context

Opening Import freezes one explicit validated ordinary destination:

  • { scope } when the main scope is displayed; or
  • { scope, sub_scope } when a configured sub-scope report or one of its validated detail documents is displayed.

That target is supplied by the app/report context owner. It is not inferred from the selected tree parent, checked IDs, title, staged filename, URL text, most recently used destination, or a package row.

The frozen target applies only to ordinary standalone documents. It is retained through preview, create, failure, retry, rebuild, and result presentation. Invalid or unavailable display context disables ordinary Import rather than falling back to the parent scope. There is no destination selector that can replace this target.

Manifest-Owned Package Routing

A trusted returned package or edited review-source folder ignores the display context for destination routing. Its associated manifest and trusted metadata must resolve one exact configured { scope } or { scope, sub_scope } collection before preview.

The modal displays that destination prominently, including when it differs from the current screen. Confirmation states the target and planned create or overwrite count. Missing, stale, ambiguous, unconfigured, capability-invalid, or cross-collection provenance blocks Import without a context fallback.

Existing semantics remain unchanged after routing:

  • returned JSON/JSONL packages retain complete package planning and their current create/overwrite and failure policy;
  • edited review-source folders remain complete, overwrite-only, stale-checked, and atomic; and
  • ordinary sources remain create-only and never gain overwrite identity from front matter.

Open In Docs Review

The selected-row secondary action is labelled Open in Docs Review.

It is enabled only when the server projects a valid returned package with supports_docs_review: true. The action uses the selected exact staged package identity to prepare or reuse its validated Docs Review package and opens the returned review URL in a safe new tab.

The button is disabled for:

  • ordinary sources;
  • edited review-source folders;
  • packages with supports_docs_review: false;
  • invalid or unassociated manifests; and
  • any candidate whose review identity cannot be resolved exactly.

The action does not select an Import target, confirm Import, or change the candidate's manifest-owned destination. Returning from Docs Review leaves Import optional.

Result And Refresh Contract

Every successful result includes one explicit destination link:

  • an ordinary create links to the exact new { scope, doc_id } or { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } document; and
  • a collection Import links to its exact owning scope or sub-scope surface.

If the destination is currently mounted, the app refreshes that exact owner. If the package imported into another collection, the current screen is not treated as its refresh target; the result link provides the explicit navigation handoff.

Result routing never falls back to the displayed document, selected parent, current report, or package title. Failure retains the selected candidate and its resolved target for a safe retry.

Entry-Point Consolidation

After behavior parity is proven:

  • retain one app-level Import action in local Manage Docs Viewer;
  • remove the sub-scope report's separate Import contribution;
  • remove the separate scope-level Review package action and chooser;
  • keep Prepare package in its selection-backed Actions workflow;
  • keep Docs Review free of Import or canonical-write controls; and
  • keep all public Docs Viewer routes unchanged and read-only.

Old controls are removed only after the consolidated route proves ordinary parent, ordinary child, returned-package, edited-folder, Review, refresh, focus, retry, and result-link parity. There is no compatibility alias that leaves two active UI owners.

Likely Authority

  • The manage app toolbar and lazy Import controller own the single entrypoint, modal lifecycle, frozen ordinary context, selected candidate, focus, busy, retry, and terminal result.
  • The staged-source listing service owns the global recognized inventory and server-projected candidate kind, manifest association, capabilities, exact target, and disabled reason.
  • The document-package profile config and review-source materializer own the shortened {timestamp}-{profile_id} file, package-id, and folder names while retaining the document-domain metadata.
  • The existing managed collection resolver owns validated display-context targets for ordinary sources.
  • Existing document-package and edited-review-source recognizers own trusted provenance, capability, membership, and manifest-routed targets.
  • Existing ordinary and collection planners retain preview, confirmation, and mutation semantics.
  • The existing Review package service owns prepare-or-reuse and returns the exact Docs Review URL.
  • Existing scope/sub-scope refresh and document-location owners provide the explicit destination result link.

These are inspection starting points, not permission to add a second target resolver or package registry.

Boundary

In scope:

  • one manage-only app-level Import entrypoint;
  • one context-independent recognized staged-source inventory;
  • removal of the Import-type and Publish-into dropdowns;
  • explicit ordinary-context versus manifest-owned target modes;
  • shortened document package file, package-id, and review-folder names;
  • exclusion of standalone media and unrelated staged files;
  • Open in Docs Review for reviewable returned packages only;
  • unchanged ordinary, returned-package, and edited-folder mutation semantics;
  • exact destination refresh and result links;
  • retirement of duplicate Import and Review package entrypoints after parity;
  • focused service, module, route, and realistic parent/Analysis-Tags evidence; and
  • durable Docs Import, Docs Review, endpoint, architecture, ownership, and Sub-Scope Index updates at closeout.

Not in scope:

  • merging or redesigning Prepare Package;
  • reviewing a staged edited review-source folder;
  • importing standalone media through Docs Import;
  • changing package schemas, capability semantics, or manifest contents;
  • migrating or retaining compatibility for already staged {timestamp}-documents-{profile_id} files and review folders;
  • changing ordinary create-only or collection atomicity rules;
  • adding public Import controls;
  • importing arbitrary or unsupported staging files;
  • automatic Import after Docs Review; or
  • using display context to filter or reroute package candidates.

Delivery Tracker

Current state: CAI-1.0 complete. Stop for review before CAI-1.1.

Review rule: complete one phase, record exact evidence beneath that phase, and stop for review before starting the next phase.

[x] CAI-1.0 — Freeze Candidate And Target Projection

  • [x] Trace current app, report, listing, package, and result-link owners; define one body-free candidate projection with ordinary-context and manifest target modes.
  • [x] List all recognized document candidates independent of display context, omit standalone media, and prove recognizer-first classification plus safe diagnostics without changing any UI entrypoint.
  • [x] Change new package files, package ids, and review folders to {timestamp}-{profile_id} names while retaining trusted document-domain metadata; require old staged artifacts to be regenerated.

CAI-1.0 implementation and evidence

  • /docs/import-source-files now returns a body-free candidates projection beside its unchanged legacy files array. Ordinary rows declare ordinary_context with no inferred target. Returned packages and complete edited review folders declare manifest_collection with the exact validated { scope } or { scope, sub_scope }, configured label, effective actions, per-action disabled reasons, and safe diagnostics.
  • The projection reuses the existing managed-collection resolver, returned-package parser and capability validation, and edited review-source recognizer. It adds no target resolver, parser, package registry, or browser inference. Source bodies, returned records, and trusted metadata payloads are not projected.
  • Review-marked folders and standalone review Markdown are claimed before ordinary Markdown listing. Complete edited folders remain Import-only; standalone reviewed files and invalid or retired folders remain visible but blocked. Trusted returned packages can independently expose Review and Import. Unassociated JSON, unsupported drop-zone files, standalone image, SVG, PDF, and other media remain absent.
  • The current app toolbar/import controller, sub-scope report contribution, type and destination controls, Review package workflow, collection terminal projection, and result refresh owners were traced but not changed. CAI-1.1 still owns the consolidated modal; CAI-1.2 still owns result links and old entrypoint removal.
  • Document package profile output now requires {timestamp}-{profile_id}.{format}. Review package and source-folder identity now derives as {timestamp}-{profile_id} while trusted metadata retains adapter_id: documents and data_domain: documents. Edited folders carrying the retired domain-bearing review id and returned packages carrying the retired domain-bearing filename fail with a regeneration diagnostic; there is no alias or migration.
  • Focused Python evidence passed 146 tests with one environment-dependent service test skipped. It covers global candidate listing, body exclusion, exact parent and child targets, per-action capability projection, blocked diagnostics, recognizer-first handling, ignored media, current listing compatibility, forward-only export/review names, ordinary and collection planning/apply, and exact sub-scope regressions.
  • Explicit Python lint passed for thirteen changed source, fixture, and test modules. Python compilation, JSON parsing, and repository whitespace validation passed. No JavaScript, HTML, public asset, Import action, Docs Review route, canonical apply, refresh, or result-link implementation changed in this phase.
  • Independent final diff review closed two candidate-boundary gaps before acceptance: multi-document Markdown folders had been advertised as ordinary one-document sources, and retired generated package filenames could still enter the existing Review/parser path. The completed review found no second target resolver, parser, package registry, body projection, context fallback, public runtime change, or CAI-1.1 modal work.

Checkpoint / review gate: review listing contents, target provenance, capability projection, blocked rows, shortened new names, and unchanged current actions before CAI-1.1.

[ ] CAI-1.1 — Build The Consolidated Modal

  • [ ] Add one app-level Import entrypoint and shared modal that freezes the ordinary display context while preserving manifest-owned package targets.
  • [ ] Remove the Import-type and Publish-into dropdowns; derive the workflow from the selected server-projected candidate and display its effective destination read-only.
  • [ ] Add selected-row Open in Docs Review enablement and prepare-or-reuse handoff for reviewable returned packages; keep ordinary and edited-folder rows disabled.

Checkpoint / review gate: review parent, sub-scope report, sub-scope detail, cross-context package, Review popup, focus, busy, cancel, and retry behavior before removing any old control.

[ ] CAI-1.2 — Consolidate Apply, Refresh, And Results

  • [ ] Route ordinary and collection preview/apply through their existing owners, refresh the exact affected destination, and provide an explicit result link even when the destination is not currently displayed.
  • [ ] Prove full behavior parity, then remove the report Import contribution and separate Review package entrypoint without leaving compatibility owners.

Checkpoint / review gate: review exact writes, cross-context refresh, destination links, old-control removal, and unchanged Prepare/Public behavior before closeout.

[ ] CAI-1.3 — Realistic Acceptance And Authority Transfer

  • [ ] Exercise ordinary parent and child sources, reviewable and import-only returned packages, edited review-source folders, blocked manifests, ignored media, shortened package names, absent type/destination selectors, review handoff, confirmation, failure/retry, and explicit result links through realistic local routes.
  • [ ] Update durable Docs Import, Docs Review, endpoint, architecture, ownership, and Sub-Scope Index documentation; rebuild Studio docs/search and independently inspect source and published projections.

Completion Gate

From either a parent scope or Analysis/Tags display, the one app-level Import modal shows the same recognized staged document inventory. An ordinary source imports into the frozen displayed collection. A returned package and an edited review-source folder import into their manifest-owned collections regardless of display context. No Import-type or Publish-into selector remains. Newly prepared package files and review folders use {timestamp}-{profile_id} names without the redundant documents segment. Open in Docs Review is available only for the reviewable returned package. Standalone media is absent. Every successful result links to the exact affected destination. Prepare Package and public routes are unchanged, and no retired Import or Review package entrypoint remains.
